axes.model_access: The platform ships no in-house model — it connects to various LLMs (OpenAI-compatible interfaces are the main axis); the hosted versions (fastgpt.io/fastgpt.cn) pre-integrate LLMs, embeddings and rerankers, with the live catalog shown in Account → Model provider by region/plan (official Model Providers page); the self-hosted version can attach local models (paired with runner-class tools).
axes.runtime: Two forms: open-source repo self-hosted (labring/FastGPT, GitHub direct 200, pushed same day 2026-10-30) + official hosted versions (fastgpt.io international direct 200; fastgpt.cn mainland direct 200, footer entity Guangzhou Huanji Cloud Computing Co., Ltd. + an ICP website registration on record, number in the cn block).
axes.local_files: In the self-hosted form data lives in your own databases (MongoDB/vector store/S3 — official Cloud vs Self-Hosted comparison); the hosted version keeps data in the official cloud, with isolated Global and China regions. Knowledge-base files are ingested and vectorized after upload; raw files and vectors live in the deployment store.
axes.background: The product's main axis is RAG knowledge-base Q&A and application orchestration (doc.fastgpt.io docs on record); FastGPT Cloud adds scheduled Dataset sync and Agent VM sandboxes (official Cloud Overview); background execution is carried by the platform.
axes.tools: The workflow-node ecosystem is on record in the docs (knowledge retrieval / HTTP request / code-execution nodes etc.); MCP works both ways: external MCP tools can be imported as tool sets (since v4.9.6; Streamable HTTP first, fallback to SSE on non-429 4xx), and FastGPT apps can be published as an MCP Server (Streamable HTTP; standalone SSE for self-hosted).
axes.context: The knowledge base (RAG) is the core persistent knowledge surface (the product's main axis); multi-turn context and variable storage are stored per application; cross-application memory is not a separately documented product surface, so no inference is made here.
axes.permissions: Open source and auditable (Apache + extra terms rather than the GPL family, see license); hosted versions follow official cloud terms; the mainland version fastgpt.cn carries an ICP registration on record; the FastGPT Cloud Privacy Policy explicitly says data is not used for additional backup storage or model training, with access/correction/deletion rights; Cloud excludes SSO and custom branding (official Cloud Overview comparison).
axes.fit: Fits: Chinese knowledge-base Q&A / RAG apps (self-hosted and controllable), a direct-mainland hosted entry (fastgpt.cn). Not a fit: wanting pure Apache 2.0 without extra terms (multi-tenant SaaS restricted), code-level agent frameworks (canvas/configuration is the main axis).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to agent platforms).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Capability gap between the hosted and self-hosted versions** (both forms run in parallel; the functional delta is not on record)
- **Knowledge-base retrieval quality and default chunking strategy** (the core quality surface of a RAG product — docs list parameters but the effect is unmeasured)
- **The live MCP/tool-calling support surface** (not verified item by item in official statements)
unknowns:
- The exact preset-model catalog on the hosted version (varies by region/plan in Account → Model provider)
- The underlying isolation parameters of the Agent VM sandbox (the official docs describe capabilities, not host-level details)
related: Also a China-origin open-source agent-building platform: Dify is the general agent canvas; FastGPT centers on RAG knowledge-base Q&A.
Also a China-origin open-source enterprise KB Q&A tool: MaxKB is GPL-3.0 with Fit2Cloud's enterprise delivery; FastGPT is Apache + extra terms with a larger community ecosystem.
